title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the unpublished continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (pages 650 bis ff.). Grothendieck is computing an explicit group scheme Z~_{rho,sigma} over Z, or over S_0. It encodes the possible 'arithmetic' automorphism data of a genus-0 configuration with S3-symmetry.

The lattice M. M is the free rank-2 module with basis lambda_0, lambda_1. From formula (60) on the previous page one reads off:
- rho(lambda_0) = lambda_1 and rho(lambda_1) = -lambda_0 - lambda_1, so rho has order 3;
- sigma swaps lambda_0 and lambda_1, so sigma has order 2.
So M is H_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) = Z^2. Here lambda_0, lambda_1 are the loops around 0 and 1, and lambda_inf = -lambda_0 - lambda_1. The S3 = <rho, sigma> action permutes the three punctures. This is the abelianization of the free profinite group that GT/Galois act on.

The map (1-rho, -(1-sigma)). The map (alpha_0, beta_0) -> (1-rho)alpha_0 - (1-sigma)beta_0 sends M x M to M. Its image is the index-3 sublattice {c_0 lambda_0 + c_1 lambda_1 : c_0 + c_1 = 0 mod 3}:
- 1-rho has determinant 3, and its image has c_0 + c_1 = 3a_1;
- the image of 1-sigma has c_0 + c_1 = 0.
The previous page first says 'surjective' and then corrects this. The Z/3 cokernel is why the kernel P (rank 2) gives a smooth vector-group scheme V(P) only away from characteristic 3, as noted on the previous page.

Arithmetic parameters. mu is in Z^* (the cyclotomic character, mu in Gamma G_m). The other parameters are nu', nu'' in Gamma G_a and nu_2, nu_3 in {0,1}. They are tied together by

 mu = 1 + 4nu' - 2nu_2 = 1 + 6nu'' - 2nu_3,

equivalently

 2nu' - nu_2 = 3nu'' - nu_3 (= (mu-1)/2).

Thus:
- nu_2 records mu mod 4, via mu = (-1)^{nu_2} mod 4;
- nu_3 records mu mod 3 (equivalently mod 6), via mu = (-1)^{nu_3} = 1 - 2nu_3;
- nu', nu'' are the lifts.
The common value (mu-1)/2 is exactly the exponent m = (lambda-1)/2 of the later GT formalism. Writing it in two ways reflects generators of order 4 and 6 in SL_2(Z), or orders 2 and 3 in PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3.

The argument on this page.
1. The general condition (from (6?) and (32)) for (mu, xi_2, xi_3) to lie in the image of Z~ -> G_m x mu_{S_0} x mu_{S_0} is 2nu' - nu_2 + nu_3 = 0 mod 3.
2. Multiply by 2 and substitute mu - 1 = 4nu' - 2nu_2. This gives mu = 1 - 2nu_3 mod 3, which holds automatically.
3. Hence the condition is redundant. Grothendieck therefore rewrites the definition: impose the integral relation 2nu' + nu_3 - nu_2 = 3nu'' directly, which defines mu = 2nu + 1.
4. Replace the abelianized cocycle equation by (1-rho)alpha_0 - (1-sigma)beta_0 = 3nu'' lambda_1. Its right side indeed lies in the image lattice, since c_0 + c_1 = 3nu''.

The result is definition (63): Z~_{rho,sigma} is a closed subgroup scheme of G_a x G_a x {0,1} x {0,1} x M x M. The next page abstracts the parameters (mu, nu', nu'', nu_2, nu_3) into a group scheme, in fact a ring scheme, D_N. It is built from the pushout of N: Z -> Z along Z -> G_a, with N = 12. This matches the fact that the abelianization of SL_2(Z) is Z/12 and that of B_3 is Z. In modern terms, the page is an abelianized (H_1-level) analysis of GT/Galois-type actions with S3-symmetry, encoded as group schemes over Z rather than profinite groups.
errors: Previous page asserts that M x M -> M is surjective. It is not: the image has index 3 (c_0 + c_1 = 0 mod 3). Grothendieck himself corrects this, and the corrected right-hand side 3nu'' lambda_1 is consistent with it.

Marginal line 'mu = 1+2nu_2+4nu'' (if read as +2nu_2) is inconsistent with the main formula mu = 4nu' - 2nu_2 + 1 and with the derived relation -nu_2 + 2nu' = -nu_3 + 3nu''. The sign is harmless mod 4 but not as an exact equality; most likely it is -2nu_2.
Next page's transcription 'mu = 3nu' - 2nu_2 + 1' must be 4nu' - 2nu_2 + 1 (either a transcription error or a slip).

ideas.what: S3-action on H_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) = Z^2 via rho (cyclic permutation of punctures) and sigma (swap of 0 and 1), and the map (1-rho, -(1-sigma)) with index-3 image, causing non-smoothness in characteristic 3
ideas.modern_name: abelianized GT cocycle conditions / H_1 of M_{0,4} with S3-symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Drinfeld (1990); Lochak-Schneps for GT actions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT idea, but not this computation

ideas.what: Writing (mu-1)/2 = 2nu' - nu_2 = 3nu'' - nu_3, with nu_2, nu_3 encoding mu mod 4 and mod 3 (orders 4 and 6 in SL_2(Z), or 2 and 3 in PSL_2)
ideas.modern_name: the exponent m = (lambda-1)/2 in GT relations; Galois/GT action on SL_2(Z)^ and B_3^

ideas.what: Encoding profinite/congruence parameters (Z^*, Z^, Z/N data) as group schemes over Z (Gamma G_m, Gamma G_a, constant {0,1}, and the ring scheme D_N with N = 12 on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: no standard name; akin to 'arithmetic group-scheme models' of profinite parameter groups

missed.claim: Pre-Drinfeld explicit computation of the abelianized (H_1-level) constraints linking the cyclotomic parameter mu with S3-symmetric conjugating data (alpha_0, beta_0) on M_{0,4}. The congruence parametrization through orders 4 and 6 later becomes the D_12 construction.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck worked out GT-type relations (including the m = (λ-1)/2 structure tied to SL_2(Z)^ab = Z/12) in a scheme-theoretic form over Z. The result is elementary, but it is relevant to the history of the GT group.

missed.claim: The group-scheme-over-Z formalism (Z~_{rho,sigma}, D_N) for profinite parameters, with its non-smoothness at characteristic 3, is set up but its purpose is not pursued in the literature.
missed.quote: Le schéma en groupes ... est lisse en car. ≠ 3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possible model for treating abelianized GT or Galois images as algebraic group schemes. It is curious but likely of limited mathematical consequence.

deep.surprise_reason: A historically interesting, explicit unpublished GT-precursor computation at abelianized level with an unusual group-scheme encoding. The mathematics itself is elementary, and its content is subsumed by the later GT / SL_2 literature.
transcription_corrections: Domain of the tuple should read G_a × G_a × {0,1}_{S_0} × {0,1}_{S_0} × M × M (nu', nu'' in Gamma G_a), not 'G_tm × G_m...'. The next page confirms nu', nu'' in Gamma G_a.
Annotation in (63) a) likely reads 'soit ν, d'où μ = 2ν+1' (ν = 2ν' − ν_2), not 'soit ν_3'.
Previous page (62): image condition is c_0 + c_1 ≡ 0 (3), with c_0 + c_1 = 3a_1 + 0, confirming the map is not surjective.
